title: Research Overview
description: This section briefly introduces my main research in artificial intelligence, including each topic, approach, and key results. Please visit the Publications page for further details.

researchStoryBridges.copy: I am currently exploring an architecture that combines compact VLA models with memory. The goal is to develop a lightweight VLA system that can use prior observations and action experience to make consistent decisions under limited computational resources.

I initially studied how to reduce inference cost and latency by reusing agent reasoning and debate traces as memory for inappropriate utterance detection. I am now extending this work to culturally grounded tasks that combine personas with RAG.

To address missing sensor data in industrial settings, I studied MARFI with a focus on MNAR, where the missingness pattern itself is informative. I completed and submitted my master's thesis on MARFI's missingness-aware imputation and its application to predictive maintenance.

Through RoboRacer, we developed autonomous racing algorithms and systems in both simulation and physical-vehicle environments. We built the full driving pipeline, from sensor-based perception to path planning and vehicle control, and repeatedly validated it across different tracks and competition settings. Our work culminated in first place at the IV 2024 competition.

items.title: Context- and Memory-Aware LLM and Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: I study LLM systems and multi-agent systems that improve inference efficiency, knowledge retrieval, and the integration of personas and contextual information. The goal is to produce reliable and consistent outputs across diverse linguistic and cultural settings.

stages.title: Memory-Enabled Reasoning
stages.copy: Agent reasoning and debate results are organized as reusable memory to reduce repetitive inference costs.

stages.title: Retrieval-Augmented Context
stages.copy: RAG retrieves external knowledge and cultural context relevant to a task and incorporates them into system responses.

stages.title: Persona-Based Agent Design
stages.copy: Agents with distinct roles and perspectives are designed to study judgment and response generation across linguistic and cultural settings.

items.title: Vision-Language-Action Research
items.summary: This research combines simulation-based task generation, Vision-Language-Action learning, and robot control for industrial mobile-manipulation tasks. It is one of the central themes of my doctoral research, and detailed methods and results will be added as the work progresses.

stages.title: Simulation and Task Generation
stages.copy: Mobile-manipulation environments are built to collect task-level trajectories for object-handling operations.

stages.title: VLA Supervised Learning
stages.copy: Models learn to connect language instructions and visual observations with predicted robot actions.

stages.title: Robustness and Sim-to-Real
stages.copy: Domain randomization, reinforcement learning, and real-world adaptation are explored to improve system robustness.

items.title: RoboRacer Autonomous Racing System
items.summary: This project uses a 1/10-scale autonomous vehicle to perceive the driving environment and detect and track dynamic obstacles in real time. Racing-line planning and vehicle-control algorithms account for the motion of nearby vehicles and are validated in both simulation and physical racing environments.

stages.title: Sensor-Based Track Perception
stages.copy: LiDAR and vehicle-state data are used to identify track boundaries and estimate the current driving state.

stages.title: Real-Time Obstacle Detection and Tracking
stages.copy: Sensor observations are used to detect nearby obstacles, track their motion over time, and assess collision risk.

stages.title: Racing-Line Planning and Control
stages.copy: The track and nearby vehicles are considered when planning the racing line and generating steering and speed commands.

stages.title: Simulation and Physical-Vehicle Validation
stages.copy: Algorithms are iteratively evaluated in simulation before their driving performance is validated on physical vehicles and in competition settings.

items.title: MNAR-Aware Imputation for Robust Predictive Maintenance
items.summary: This research focuses on MNAR settings in predictive-maintenance sensor data, where the missingness pattern itself is informative. MARFI analyzes missingness patterns and co-missing relationships, then learns the missingness mechanism through remasking and auxiliary mask prediction. It preserves observed values while reconstructing only missing positions and evaluates both distribution fidelity and downstream predictive-maintenance performance.

items.alt: Missingness masks, feature correlations, and quantile profiles
Imputation-error comparison across missingness mechanisms and ratios
Comparison of reconstructed and ground-truth feature distributions
Language-model-assisted classification architecture for missing sensor data
Downstream prediction accuracy across missing-data scenarios

stages.title: MNAR Missingness Analysis
stages.copy: Missingness masks, co-missing relationships across sensors, and value quantiles are analyzed to characterize non-random missingness associated with the data itself.

stages.title: Remasking-Based Mechanism Learning
stages.copy: Remasking hides a subset of observed values to construct training signals, while auxiliary mask prediction learns missingness patterns embedded in the data.

stages.title: Mask-Conditioned Imputation
stages.copy: A rectified-flow velocity field is conditioned on the missingness mask to reconstruct only missing sensor positions without modifying observed values.

stages.title: Distribution and Downstream Validation
stages.copy: Reconstruction error and distribution fidelity are compared across missingness mechanisms and ratios, together with the effect of imputed data on equipment-state prediction.
